Operating Characteristics of the U-BOIN Design

Source: R/sim_uboin.R
sim_uboin.Rd

Simulate a trial run with the utility-based BOIN (U-BOIN) phase I/II design of Zhou, Lee and Yuan (2019) many times under one scenario of true DLT and response probabilities, and summarize how often each dose is selected as the optimal biological dose (OBD), how many patients are treated at each dose and how many DLTs and responses are observed.

Usage

sim_uboin(
  tox_upper,
  resp_lower,
  p_true = NULL,
  p_resp = NULL,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  target = NULL,
  resp_assoc = 0,
  p_outcome = NULL,
  utility = c(0, 30, 50, 100),
  n_stage1 = 12,
  n_stop = NULL,
  start_dose = 1,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  prior_tox = c(1, 1),
  prior_resp = c(1, 1),
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

tox_upper

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, for example 0.30.

resp_lower

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, for example 0.20.

p_true

Numeric vector or NULL. True DLT probability of each dose.

p_resp

Numeric vector or NULL. True response probability of each dose.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial; the maximum sample size is n_cohort * cohort_size.

cohort_size

Integer scalar. Number of patients per cohort.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

target

Numeric scalar or NULL. Target DLT probability of the BOIN design in stage I. Defaults to NULL, which uses tox_upper - 0.05.

resp_assoc

Numeric scalar. Association parameter of the Gumbel model that joins the DLT and the response of a patient; 0 makes them independent. Defaults to 0.

p_outcome

Numeric matrix or NULL. Probabilities of the four outcomes of a patient at each dose, one row per dose, in the columns (no response, DLT), (no response, no DLT), (response, DLT) and (response, no DLT). When given, p_true, p_resp and resp_assoc must be NULL or are not used. Defaults to NULL.

utility

Numeric vector of length four. Utility of the four outcomes, in the order of p_outcome. Defaults to c(0, 30, 50, 100), example 1 of the article.

n_stage1

Integer scalar. Stage II starts once a dose has this many patients (s1 of the article). Defaults to 12.

n_stop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial ends once a dose has this many patients (s2 of the article). Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level of the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is toxic when the posterior probability that its DLT probability exceeds tox_upper is above this value. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is futile when the posterior probability that its response probability is below resp_lower is above this value. Defaults to 0.90.

prior_tox

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the DLT probability in the toxicity rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

prior_resp

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the response probability in the futility rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the trial by trial data in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress while the simulation runs. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class uboin_oc, which is a list with components

sel_percent

Percentage of trials selecting each dose as the OBD.

percent_no_obd

Percentage of trials without an OBD, which the article calls the percentage of early stopping.

n_pts_dose, n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Average numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at each dose.

total_n_pts, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their totals.

true_utility

True mean utility of each dose, p_outcome %*% utility.

percent_stage2

Percentage of trials that reached stage II.

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials by reason for ending.

trials, obd

The trials and their OBDs when keep_trials is TRUE.

together with the design parameters and the call.

Details

The trials are simulated with uboin_simulate, whose help page describes the rules, and the OBD is selected with uboin_select_obd: the admissible dose with the largest posterior mean utility at the end of the trial. A trial stopped because the lowest dose was eliminated or no dose was admissible selects none.

With resp_assoc = 0.2, cohorts of 3, n_cohort = 18, tox_upper = 0.30, resp_lower = 0.20 and the other defaults, the results agree with Table 3 of the article and Table S9 of its supporting information within simulation error (inst/reproduce/reproduce_Zhou2019.R).

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J. and Yuan, Y. (2019). A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval (U-BOIN) phase I/II design to identify the optimal biological dose for targeted and immune therapies. Statistics in Medicine, 38(28), S5299-S5316. doi:10.1002/sim.8361

See also

sim_uboin_multi, uboin_simulate, uboin_select_obd, uboin_utility_table

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Simulation A of the article
oc <- sim_uboin(
  tox_upper = 0.30,
  resp_lower = 0.20,
  p_true = c(0.02, 0.15, 0.30, 0.45, 0.60),
  p_resp = c(0.20, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65),
  n_cohort = 18,
  cohort_size = 3,
  resp_assoc = 0.2,
  n_trials = 500,
  seed = 123
)
oc
